scope: Relative and endogenous value function iteration for finite MDPs: the span seminorm and the Dobrushin bound; constant-shift invariance of the Bellman operator and of greedy policies (White), relative value iteration as value iteration up to a constant, the span contraction sp(Tv - Tw) <= beta alpha sp(v - w); strong convergence of relative values at rate beta alpha, the MacQueen-Porteus policy error bound, Bray's stopping rule and its finite termination; White's average-reward theorem (beta = 1, alpha < 1): convergence to a solution of the average-reward optimality equation, optimality and uniqueness of the gain; endogenous value iteration for exogenous/endogenous state splits (Bray): invariance to exogenous shifts, the endogenizing operator, the within-x span contraction at rate beta alpha_y with alpha_y bounded by the full Dobrushin bound, recovery of v* and optimal policies from the endogenous value, the policy error bound, and an example where relative VFI gives no speed-up but endogenous VFI is exact; asymptotic eigenvalue rates: spectral radius of real matrices and Gelfand's formula, the subradius rho(Delta Q) as the second-largest eigenvalue modulus (no Jordan block at 1) bounded by the Dobrushin coefficient, freezing of the greedy policy at a unique optimal decision rule, the Morton-Wecker rate beta lambda(P*) for relative values and Morton's rate for policy evaluation, levels no faster than beta, and the endogenous rates beta rho(Lambda P) with rho(Lambda F) <= lambda(F) (Bray); when endogenous VFI is strictly faster (Bray): every eigenvalue of Delta_X F_x is one of Delta P so sigma(F_x) <= sigma(P), rho(Lambda P) bounded by any vector-norm operator bound on Omega F_y(x), the Frobenius, largest-singular-value, row-sum, column-sum and Hajnal instances (with the largest singular value as the l2 operator norm), non-ergodic F_x with scrambling F_y, and x-independent F_y with sigma(F_x) > sigma(F_y); and rho(Omega F) = sigma(F) for every stochastic F (Bray, Lemma 7); relative and endogenous policy iteration (Bray): the same policies as policy iteration, policy improvement and finite termination, the endogenous policy error bound beta/(1 - beta) sp(Lambda(Tw - w)), and Bray's stopping rules returning epsilon-optimal policies after finitely many iterations.
source: White (1963); Morton (1971); Morton and Wecker (1977); MacQueen (1966); Porteus (1971); Seneta (1981); Puterman (2005); Bray (2019, Quantitative Economics); Bray (2019, Management Science); Hajnal (1958); Horn and Johnson (2013); Howard (1960).
